\cvsection{Space systems}

\job{VOLLEY, an electromagnetic orbital CubeSat deployer}{Independent, final-year project \textbullet\ IEEE manuscript in preparation}{2021--present}
\begin{tight}
  \item Architected a magazine-fed \textbf{ironless double-sided Halbach linear synchronous motor}
        that ejects \textbf{unmodified} 3U CubeSats at \textbf{16.5\,m/s} (13.1--18.5\,m/s
        across the 1U--12U family) at \textbf{10.7\,g} on \textbf{2.58\,kJ} per shot ---
        eight times a spring, inside standard CubeSat qualification loads.
  \item Selected the LSM over a coilgun in a documented architecture trade: a coilgun needs a
        conductive armature on the customer satellite, and its velocity advantage is capped by the
        payload's own g-limit. Verified against published work reaching 321\,m/s at
        $\sim$1350\,g --- roughly 100$\times$ CubeSat qualification.
  \item Derived the thrust constant \textbf{11.22\,N per kA/m} from a winding-resolved model, then
        \textbf{wrote a 2-D magnetostatic FEM from the weak form} (scikit-fem, gmsh, 141k elements)
        to check it independently: agreement to \textbf{0.07\,\%}.
  \item Closed the system at \textbf{77\,kg dry}, and \textbf{published every defect found}
        --- 46 numbered open problems, with acceptance bands declared before each analysis ran.
        \textbf{Retracted my own claims when evidence went against them}: an independent propagator
        (GMAT) falsified a claim in the paper's abstract; my cost model contradicted the paper on
        which parts dominate; a literature review found prior art I had missed. Presented at
        \textbf{DRDO ARDE}, Pune (2021) and the \textbf{India Science Festival}, IISER Pune (2024).
\end{tight}

\job{Electromagnetic Launch System for Vertical Silo-Based Deployment}{Sole author \textbullet\ feasibility study, IEEE format}{2025}
\begin{tight}
  \item Applied the same magazine-fed electromagnetic launch architecture to a 500\,kg booster
        class: belt-feed indexing, pulsed coilgun ejection, ignition deferred to 20\,m altitude.
        \textbf{2.50--4.17\,MJ per launch} across a sourced 15--25\,\% efficiency band,
        \textbf{10.6--15.0 cycles/min} on a 1\,MW supply.
  \item \textbf{Selected a coilgun here and rejected one for the CubeSat deployer} --- the same
        trade, resolved oppositely, because both are sized by the payload's g-limit via
        $s_{\min}=v^2/2ng$. A 15\,m rail holds 8.5\,g against a 10--15\,g propellant grain; a
        1.5\,m track holds 10.7\,g against a 14\,g CubeSat. Two machines, one constraint.
\end{tight}

\job{Re-entry Parachute Deployment System}{IREC 2025, Team THRUST \textbullet\ Midland, Texas}{2025}
\begin{tight}
  \item \textbf{2nd place globally}, SDL Payload Challenge. Modelled aerodynamic drag, engineered
        structural reliability into the recovery mechanism, and validated the deployment sequence
        against failure modes (FMEA).
\end{tight}
